target_customer: Banks, retailers, fintechs and apps in Latin America that want to offer bill pay and payments (originally: US immigrants paying bills for family in Mexico and the Dominican Republic)
problem: Paying bills and services in Latin America was fragmented and cash-based; remittance and payment products were expensive, and businesses needed one API to reach billers across countries.
business_model: B2B payments-as-a-service API and biller network; originally a consumer bill-pay app with a flat $2.99 fee per automatic payment

founders.name: Iñigo Rumayor
prior_employers: Regalii (co-founded; CRO/COO roles per YC page)
previous_startups: Regalii (the company that became Arcus, per aggregator and YC page; separate entity not established)
founders.background_notes: Spelled Iñigo Rumayor on the YC page; one aggregator profile says Iñigo Martinez.

founders.name: Edrizio De La Cruz
founders.background_notes: A 2014 profile describes him as a Dominican immigrant who built the remittance startup.

founders.name: Juan Maldonado
prior_employers: Financial empowerment center for NYC Mayor Bloomberg's administration
founders.background_notes: Built the international team and led hiring per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating with many biller systems, retailers and later Mexico's SPEI rails for a small team in 2013-2014 was integration-heavy and compliance-heavy, but not research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: Direct biller and retailer connections across several countries, bank clients (BBVA, Santander) and payment licensing approvals were slow to copy, but the 2013 consumer app wedge itself was easy to imitate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent remittance firms partnered rather than copied (Ria and IDT partnered with Regalii per 2015 coverage); Mastercard bought the later infrastructure business in November 2021.

market_need_then: Immigrants paid high fees to send money home, and the 2014 coverage quoted founders calling money-transfer services very expensive; no hard demand figures found.

branding.domain_note: Brand was originally Regalii (regalii.com); arcusfi.com used later.
branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage of the founders' immigrant story (TechCrunch, PBS NewsHour, Latin Post) but nothing about the brand itself.

brand_strength.rationale: A B2B infrastructure name with no sourced identity assets; search results are crowded with unrelated 'Arcus' and 'Arrcus' companies, and no brand-driven growth is documented.

pivots.from: Consumer remittance app for sending money to family
pivots.to: Consumer bill pay for family abroad (Mexico, Dominican Republic)
pivots.why: Not sourced; 2014 coverage describes the bill-pay product

pivots.to: B2B white-label bill pay and payments platform for remittance providers and businesses
pivots.why: Not sourced; American Banker (2015) and a 2016 press release describe the B2B model

outcome_analysis: Arcus began in the Summer 2013 batch as the remittance and bill-pay app Regalii, pivoted toward white-label and B2B payments, took money from a16z, Kapor, Initialized, Ignia, Citi Ventures and SoftBank's fund, and grew into a bill-pay and cash-in network used by banks and large retailers in Mexico. Mastercard acquired it in November 2021 after about eight years, which counts as a strategic exit with undisclosed price; the pivot from a thin consumer wedge to integration-heavy infrastructure with bank clients and rail approvals is the main reason it reached an exit.
notes: Announcement date: Mastercard press release and Payments Dive are dated 2021-11-24; the YC founder bio says December 3, 2021, so 2021-11 used. Price undisclosed. Funding unverified (not recorded as rounds): an aggregator (StartupIntros) lists a $2M seed in 2013-12 and an $8M Series A in 2017-12 with no investors; Payments Dive cites Crunchbase for $19.7M across five rounds; Latin Post (2014) says $2.7M raised since launch; investors named in sources include a16z, Winklevoss Capital, Maverick, Kapor, Initialized, Ignia, Citi Ventures, SB Opportunity Fund. The YC page and sources link Regalii to Arcus (same Crunchbase record, Regalii coverage in 2014-2016); the rename date and reason are not stated in sources read. YC page says Summer 2013 though one search summary said Winter 2013. A later sale to Tapi in 2025 was mentioned only in one search summary and is not verified. Competition: no competitors named in any dated 2013-2015 source read (tech.co, American Banker, PRNewswire), so list left empty. Finextra returned 403 and was not worked around. Web Archive skipped. Completeness pass: the 2013 seed (Fenox Venture Capital, amount undisclosed) and the 2017 round ($7.9M) rest on a single outlet, Global Corporate Venturing. StartupIntros calls them a $2M seed (2013-12) and an $8M Series A (2017-12); amounts conflict and the StartupIntros figures were not recorded. Totals raised conflict: $16M as of Nov 2020 (Global Corporate Venturing), $19.7M over five rounds (Payments Dive citing Crunchbase), $25.5M over 14 rounds (CB Insights), so the recorded rounds are an incomplete history.
